subject: Quantaflow: Rapid throughput & latency degradation — coordination
messages:
From: Sam Dorsey <sam.dorsey@quantaflow.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: anna.kim@quantaflow.com
Date: 2028-05-16T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Sharp spike in 5xx and tail latency on /generate endpoint

Monica —

We're seeing a sudden spike in 5xx errors and p95/p99 latency on our /generate calls starting ~08:45 PT. Throughput is nominal but request-level latencies have doubled and a subset of requests are timing out. Our app is experiencing user-visible failures in production (majority traffic routed to your hosted endpoint).

Key facts: 
- Start: ~08:45 PT
- Error rate visible in our dashboard: 4.7% (baseline ~0.1%)
- P95 latency: 2.2s -> 5.1s; P99: 4.8s -> 12s
- No config changes on our side.

I've attached a small sample of request IDs and traces. Can you confirm if there are active incidents on your side and what the immediate mitigation plan is? We need a readout for our incident channel and expected timeline.

Thanks,
Sam
Customer Success — QuantaFlow
[sample attachment: qflow-traces_1605.csv]

From: monica.patel@redwood.com
To: Sam Dorsey <sam.dorsey@quantaflow.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-16T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sharp spike in 5xx and tail latency on /generate endpoint

Sam — thanks for the heads up and the traces. We're pulling a rapid bridge now and will triage immediately. Initial ask: can you confirm one affected request ID in the CSV we can correlate?

I've looped in Marcus (runtime lead) and Vivek (capacity/infra) to investigate KV cache behavior, routing and any backend degradation. We'll: 
- Triage traces and request IDs
- Check model variant routing and fallback activity
- Review recent autoscaling events and GPU pool health

I'll follow up with an estimated ETA for an initial update within 30 minutes. Please hold any config changes on your side until we confirm.

— Monica
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

[attachment referenced: latency-samples_20280516.log]

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: monica.patel@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Sam Dorsey <sam.dorsey@quantaflow.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sharp spike in 5xx and tail latency on /generate endpoint

I have an initial signal from the serving plane: increased KV cache miss rate on the shard serving QuantaFlow's traffic, which aligns with a rollback of a cache eviction heuristic that ran at 08:42 PT. That change created transient cache pressure across a subset of hosts; most requests should have fallen back to slower KV read paths which explains p99 spikes and 5xxs for bursts.

Immediate actions I'm executing now: 
- Reverting the eviction heuristic change to the previous stable profile (rolling, expected 3–5min to reach all hosts)
- Forcing prefix cache warm on the most impacted model shard (kick warmers)
- Temporarily increasing routing affinity to avoid cold-hosts for QuantaFlow traffic while rollout completes

I'll post status in 10 minutes. If warmers don't bring down p99 we should enable graceful fallback to a lower-latency model variant for their production traffic (requires Monica approval).

— Marcus
Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: monica.patel@redwood.com
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: Sam Dorsey <sam.dorsey@quantaflow.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T09:36:00-07:00
Subject: Exec bridge (15m) + customer update: Quantaflow incident

Team — short bridge in 15 minutes to align execs and confirm next steps. Marcus, Vivek: confirm revert window and whether we need to escalate to infra (scheduling kernel-level restart on 3 hosts). Rachel: I'm bringing you into the loop for executive comms and potential SLA credit discussion.

Sam — quick update for QuantaFlow's ops channel: we observed a cache eviction heuristic rollback at 08:42 PT that correlates with your traces. We're reverting the change and warming affected hosts; expected stabilization in ~10–15 minutes. If we do not see improvement we'll enable a temporary model-variant fallback to reduce tail latency. Will confirm again at T+30.

Meeting link: https://meet.redwood.com/bridges/quantaflow-1605 (joining in 15)

— Monica
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

[attachment referenced: kv-cache-dump-05-16.tar.gz]

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: monica.patel@redwood.com, rachel.kim@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-16T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-bridge status: stabilization in progress

Post-bridge summary: 
- Revert completed across all affected hosts by 09:58 PT. 
- Cache warmers running; overall p95 down from 5.1s to 1.9s, p99 improved from 12s to ~3.4s on observed sample.
- 5xxs reduced to 0.3% and continuing to decline.

Remaining work and asks: 
- Continue warmers for +20m to fully repopulate prefix state.
- Monitor for residual tail spikes during high burst windows; consider keeping routing affinity adjusted for next 2 hours.
- Prepare rollback note and RCA draft for later.

If metrics are stable at T+45 we can draft a customer-facing timeline and close the bridge.

— Marcus
Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: monica.patel@redwood.com
To: Sam Dorsey <sam.dorsey@quantaflow.com>, Anna Kim <anna.kim@quantaflow.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, rachel.kim@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-16T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Quantaflow production update — resolved (interim)

Sam / Anna —

Final update from our side: the cache eviction rollback + aggressive warmers stabilized the tail latency and error rate. Timeline: 
- Incident start: ~08:45 PT
- Mitigation (revert started): 08:47 PT
- Stabilized (observed improvement): ~09:58 PT
- Monitoring window completed and no recurrence: 15:40 PT

Outcome: 5xx rate returned to baseline (~0.08%), p95/p99 within expected SLAs. We've scheduled a follow-up RCA and change control review: expected draft by EOD tomorrow.

Next steps for QuantaFlow: 
- We'll share the RCA and a proposed change control checklist to avoid auto-eviction rollbacks impacting production in the future.
- If you'd like, we can provision a dedicated warm-up profile for your traffic.

Thanks for your patience and for providing the trace samples — that sped up correlation. If you need a written incident report for your internal compliance threads let me know and we'll prioritize it.

— Monica
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
